vitreous body.summary: The clear jelly filling the back of the eyeball.
vitreous body.function: Keeps the eyeball inflated and holds the retina in place.
vitreous body.clinical: Its shrinking with age causes floaters and can tear the retina.

optic part of retina.summary: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
optic part of retina.function: Rods and cones convert light into nerve signals sent along the optic nerve.
optic part of retina.clinical: Retinal detachment, diabetic retinopathy and macular degeneration.

anterior chamber of eyeball.summary: The fluid-filled space between the cornea and the iris.
anterior chamber of eyeball.function: Filled with aqueous humour that nourishes the cornea and lens.
anterior chamber of eyeball.clinical: Blocked drainage of aqueous humour raises pressure in glaucoma.

corona ciliaris.summary: The folded front part of the ciliary body behind the iris.
corona ciliaris.function: Produces aqueous humour and suspends the lens.

suspensory ligament of lens.summary: The zonular fibres holding the lens in place.
suspensory ligament of lens.function: Transmit the pull of the ciliary muscle to change the shape of the lens.

lacrimal gland.summary: The almond-shaped gland in the upper outer corner of the orbit.
lacrimal gland.function: Produces tears that wash and protect the eye.

lacrimal lake.summary: The pool of tears in the inner corner of the eye.

lacrimal canaliculus.summary: A tiny channel draining tears from the eyelid margin to the lacrimal sac.

lacrimal sac.summary: The upper dilated part of the tear drainage duct in the inner orbit.
lacrimal sac.clinical: Infection (dacryocystitis) causes a painful swelling beside the nose.

nasolacrimal duct.summary: The duct carrying tears from the lacrimal sac into the nose.
nasolacrimal duct.clinical: Blockage causes a constantly watering eye.

tarsal plate of upper eyelid.summary: The firm plate of connective tissue giving the upper eyelid its shape.

tarsal plate of lower eyelid.summary: The firm plate of connective tissue giving the lower eyelid its shape.

check ligament of lateral rectus.summary: A band of fascia limiting the pull of the lateral rectus muscle.

check ligament of medial rectus.summary: A band of fascia limiting the pull of the medial rectus muscle.

trochlea of superior oblique.summary: The fibrocartilage pulley on the roof of the orbit through which the superior oblique tendon passes.

external ear.summary: The auricle (pinna): the visible ear of skin-covered elastic cartilage.
external ear.function: Collects sound and funnels it into the ear canal; its shape helps locate sounds.

wall of left atrium.summary: The thin muscular wall of the left atrium, which receives oxygenated blood from the four pulmonary veins.
wall of left atrium.function: Contracts to top up the left ventricle just before it pumps.
wall of left atrium.clinical: Atrial fibrillation can let clots form here, a major cause of stroke.

wall of right atrium.summary: The wall of the right atrium, which receives venous blood from the venae cavae and coronary sinus.
wall of right atrium.function: Houses the sinoatrial node, the heart's natural pacemaker.

wall of ventricle.summary: The thick muscular walls of the two ventricles and the septum between them; the left wall is about three times thicker than the right.
wall of ventricle.function: Contract to pump blood to the lungs (right) and the body (left).
wall of ventricle.clinical: Heart attacks damage this muscle; the left ventricle thickens in high blood pressure.

cavity of left ventricle.summary: The chamber of the left ventricle, which pumps blood into the aorta.
cavity of left ventricle.clinical: Its ejection fraction is the standard measure of heart function.

cavity of right ventricle.summary: The chamber of the right ventricle, which pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk.

cavity of left atrium.summary: The chamber receiving oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.

cavity of right atrium.summary: The chamber receiving deoxygenated blood from the body.

anterior leaflet of mitral valve.summary: The larger of the two leaflets of the mitral valve between the left atrium and ventricle.
anterior leaflet of mitral valve.function: Swings shut during ventricular contraction to stop blood flowing back into the atrium.

posterior leaflet of mitral valve.summary: The smaller, crescent-shaped leaflet of the mitral valve.
posterior leaflet of mitral valve.function: Meets the anterior leaflet to seal the valve.

anterior leaflet of tricuspid valve.summary: The largest leaflet of the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and ventricle.

posterior leaflet of tricuspid valve.summary: One of the three leaflets of the tricuspid valve.

septal leaflet of tricuspid valve.summary: The leaflet of the tricuspid valve attached to the interventricular septum.

anterior papillary muscle of right ventr.summary: The largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle.
anterior papillary muscle of right ventr.function: Its chordae tendineae stop the tricuspid leaflets flipping back into the atrium.

posterior papillary muscle of right vent.summary: A papillary muscle on the floor of the right ventricle anchoring the tricuspid valve.

septal papillary muscle of right ventric.summary: A small papillary muscle arising from the septum of the right ventricle.

lateral papillary muscle of left ventric.summary: One of the two large papillary muscles of the left ventricle anchoring the mitral valve.
lateral papillary muscle of left ventric.clinical: Rupture after a heart attack causes sudden severe mitral regurgitation.

anterolateral head of lateral papillary.summary: A head of the anterolateral papillary muscle of the left ventricle.

anterior cusp of pulmonary valve.summary: One of the three half-moon cusps of the pulmonary valve at the outlet of the right ventricle.
anterior cusp of pulmonary valve.function: Prevents blood returning from the pulmonary trunk during diastole.

left anterior cusp of pulmonary valve.summary: One of the three cusps of the pulmonary valve.

right anterior cusp of pulmonary valve.summary: One of the three cusps of the pulmonary valve.

posterior cusp of pulmonary valve.summary: One of the three cusps of the pulmonary valve.

ascending aorta.summary: The first 5 cm of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle behind the pulmonary trunk.
ascending aorta.function: Gives off the two coronary arteries just above the aortic valve.
ascending aorta.clinical: Aortic dissection most often begins here.

arch of aorta.summary: The curved part of the aorta arching over the heart and left main bronchus.
arch of aorta.function: Gives rise to the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.
arch of aorta.clinical: Contains baroreceptors that sense blood pressure.

thoracic aorta.summary: The descending aorta as it runs down the chest beside the vertebral column.
thoracic aorta.function: Supplies the chest wall, oesophagus and bronchi through its branches.

abdominal aorta.summary: The aorta from the diaphragm to its division into the common iliac arteries at L4.
abdominal aorta.function: Supplies the abdominal organs, kidneys and the lower limbs.
abdominal aorta.clinical: Abdominal aortic aneurysms are screened for in older men.

aorta.summary: The largest artery in the body, carrying blood from the left ventricle to the whole systemic circulation.
aorta.clinical: Aneurysm and dissection are life-threatening emergencies.

pulmonary trunk.summary: The short wide artery from the right ventricle that divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.
pulmonary trunk.function: Carries deoxygenated blood toward the lungs.

common carotid artery.summary: The main artery of the neck, dividing at the level of the thyroid cartilage into internal and external carotids.
common carotid artery.clinical: The carotid pulse is felt beside the larynx; atheroma at its division causes strokes.

internal carotid artery.summary: The artery entering the skull to supply the brain and eye.
internal carotid artery.function: Feeds the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and the ophthalmic artery.
internal carotid artery.clinical: Narrowing (stenosis) is treated by endarterectomy or stenting to prevent stroke.

external carotid artery.summary: The artery supplying the face, scalp, jaw and neck.
external carotid artery.function: Its branches include the facial, lingual, maxillary and superficial temporal arteries.

vertebral artery.summary: An artery from the subclavian that climbs through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae into the skull.
vertebral artery.function: The two vertebral arteries join to form the basilar artery supplying the brainstem and cerebellum.
vertebral artery.clinical: Dissection can follow neck manipulation or trauma.

basilar artery.summary: The single artery formed by the two vertebral arteries on the front of the pons.
basilar artery.function: Supplies the brainstem, cerebellum and occipital lobes.

middle cerebral artery.summary: The largest branch of the internal carotid artery, running through the lateral fissure.
middle cerebral artery.function: Supplies the lateral surface of the hemisphere, including the motor, sensory and language areas.
middle cerebral artery.clinical: The commonest site of ischaemic stroke.

anterior cerebral artery.summary: A branch of the internal carotid supplying the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes.
anterior cerebral artery.clinical: Occlusion weakens the opposite leg more than the arm.

posterior cerebral artery.summary: The terminal branch of the basilar artery supplying the occipital lobe.
posterior cerebral artery.clinical: Occlusion causes loss of the opposite visual field.

subclavian artery.summary: The artery under the clavicle supplying the arm, neck and brain (via the vertebral artery).
subclavian artery.function: Becomes the axillary artery at the outer border of the first rib.

axillary artery.summary: The continuation of the subclavian artery through the armpit.
axillary artery.function: Supplies the shoulder and becomes the brachial artery.

brachial artery.summary: The main artery of the upper arm, running along the inner side of the biceps.
brachial artery.function: Divides at the elbow into the radial and ulnar arteries.
brachial artery.clinical: The artery used to measure blood pressure.

radial artery.summary: The artery of the thumb side of the forearm.
radial artery.clinical: Felt as the pulse at the wrist; used for arterial blood sampling and cardiac catheterisation.

ulnar artery.summary: The larger of the two forearm arteries, on the little-finger side.
ulnar artery.function: Forms the superficial palmar arch supplying the fingers.

superficial palmar arch.summary: The arterial arch across the palm formed mainly by the ulnar artery.
superficial palmar arch.function: Gives off the digital arteries to the fingers.

deep palmar arch.summary: The arterial arch deep in the palm formed mainly by the radial artery.

celiac trunk.summary: The first major branch of the abdominal aorta, dividing into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries.
celiac trunk.function: Supplies the stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas and duodenum.

common hepatic artery.summary: A branch of the coeliac trunk supplying the liver, gallbladder, stomach and duodenum.

hepatic artery proper.summary: The artery entering the liver alongside the portal vein and bile duct.
hepatic artery proper.function: Provides about a quarter of the liver's blood supply, rich in oxygen.

splenic artery.summary: The largest and most tortuous branch of the coeliac trunk, running along the top of the pancreas to the spleen.

superior mesenteric artery.summary: The artery supplying the small intestine and the first half of the colon.
superior mesenteric artery.clinical: Occlusion causes bowel infarction, a surgical emergency.

inferior mesenteric artery.summary: The artery supplying the descending and sigmoid colon and the rectum.

renal artery.summary: The large artery from the aorta to each kidney.
renal artery.function: Carries a fifth of the cardiac output through the kidneys for filtration.
renal artery.clinical: Narrowing (renal artery stenosis) causes high blood pressure.

testicular artery.summary: A long slender artery from the aorta to the testis, travelling in the spermatic cord.

common iliac artery.summary: One of the two terminal branches of the aorta, dividing into internal and external iliac arteries.

external iliac artery.summary: The artery running along the pelvic brim to become the femoral artery under the inguinal ligament.

internal iliac artery.summary: The artery supplying the pelvic organs, buttock and perineum.

femoral artery.summary: The main artery of the thigh, entering below the inguinal ligament.
femoral artery.function: Supplies the lower limb; its deep branch feeds the thigh muscles.
femoral artery.clinical: The femoral pulse is felt in the groin; it is the usual access point for catheter procedures.

deep femoral artery.summary: The largest branch of the femoral artery, supplying the thigh muscles and the head of the femur.

popliteal artery.summary: The continuation of the femoral artery behind the knee.
popliteal artery.clinical: Vulnerable in knee dislocations; aneurysms occur here.

anterior tibial artery.summary: The artery of the front of the leg, becoming the dorsalis pedis on top of the foot.
anterior tibial artery.clinical: The dorsalis pedis pulse checks circulation to the foot.

posterior tibial artery.summary: The main artery of the back of the leg, passing behind the inner ankle into the sole.
posterior tibial artery.clinical: Its pulse behind the medial malleolus is checked in vascular examination.

fibular artery.summary: A branch of the posterior tibial artery along the fibula supplying the lateral leg.

left coronary artery.summary: The artery from the left aortic sinus that divides into the anterior interventricular (left anterior descending) and circumflex branches.
left coronary artery.function: Supplies most of the left ventricle and the septum.
left coronary artery.clinical: Narrowing of its main stem is the most dangerous form of coronary disease.

right coronary artery.summary: The artery from the right aortic sinus running in the groove between the right atrium and ventricle.
right coronary artery.function: Supplies the right ventricle, the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes and usually the back of the left ventricle.
right coronary artery.clinical: Blockage causes inferior heart attacks, often with slow heart rhythms.

anterior interventricular branch of left.summary: The left anterior descending artery running down the front of the heart between the ventricles.
anterior interventricular branch of left.function: Supplies the front of the left ventricle and most of the septum.
anterior interventricular branch of left.clinical: Its blockage causes the classic anterior heart attack, the so-called widow-maker.

circumflex branch of left coronary arter.summary: The branch of the left coronary curving round the left side of the heart.
circumflex branch of left coronary arter.function: Supplies the lateral and back wall of the left ventricle.

posterior interventricular branch of rig.summary: The branch running down the back of the heart between the ventricles, usually from the right coronary artery.

marginal branch of right coronary artery.summary: A branch running along the lower border of the heart to supply the right ventricle.

coronary sinus.summary: The large vein on the back of the heart collecting most of the cardiac veins into the right atrium.

great cardiac vein.summary: The vein accompanying the anterior interventricular artery and draining into the coronary sinus.

middle cardiac vein.summary: The vein accompanying the posterior interventricular artery on the back of the heart.

small cardiac vein.summary: A vein along the right border of the heart draining into the coronary sinus.

anterior interventricular vein.summary: The vein beside the left anterior descending artery, beginning the great cardiac vein.

posterior vein of left ventricle.summary: A vein draining the back of the left ventricle into the coronary sinus.

superior vena cava.summary: The large vein returning blood from the head, neck, arms and chest to the right atrium.
superior vena cava.clinical: Compression by a lung tumour causes facial swelling (SVC syndrome).

inferior vena cava.summary: The largest vein in the body, returning blood from the legs, pelvis and abdomen to the right atrium.
inferior vena cava.clinical: Filters can be placed in it to catch clots from the leg veins.

brachiocephalic vein.summary: The vein formed by the internal jugular and subclavian veins behind the sternoclavicular joint; the two join to form the superior vena cava.

internal jugular vein.summary: The large vein draining the brain, face and neck, running beside the carotid artery.
internal jugular vein.clinical: Its pressure, seen as the jugular venous pulse, reflects the filling of the right heart; a common site for central lines.

external jugular vein.summary: The superficial vein crossing the sternocleidomastoid, draining the scalp and face.

subclavian vein.summary: The vein under the clavicle continuing the axillary vein.
subclavian vein.clinical: Used for central venous access; the thoracic duct empties into its junction with the jugular on the left.

axillary vein.summary: The vein of the armpit continuing the basilic vein toward the subclavian.

cephalic vein.summary: The superficial vein running up the outer arm to the shoulder.
cephalic vein.clinical: Used for intravenous lines and pacemaker leads.

basilic vein.summary: The superficial vein running up the inner arm to become the axillary vein.

median cubital vein.summary: The vein crossing the front of the elbow joining the cephalic and basilic veins.
median cubital vein.clinical: The usual site for taking blood.

median antebrachial vein.summary: A superficial vein of the front of the forearm.

brachial vein.summary: The deep veins accompanying the brachial artery in the upper arm.

radial vein.summary: Deep veins accompanying the radial artery.

ulnar vein.summary: Deep veins accompanying the ulnar artery.

azygos vein.summary: A vein running up the right side of the thoracic spine into the superior vena cava.
azygos vein.function: Drains the chest wall and provides a bypass if the venae cavae are blocked.

hemiazygos vein.summary: The left-sided partner of the azygos vein, crossing to join it in the mid-chest.

portal vein.summary: The vein carrying nutrient-rich blood from the intestines, stomach, spleen and pancreas into the liver.
portal vein.function: Delivers about three quarters of the liver's blood for processing before it reaches the general circulation.
portal vein.clinical: Cirrhosis raises pressure in the portal system, causing varices and ascites.

pre-hepatic portal vein.summary: The trunk of the portal vein before it enters the liver.

hepatic vein.summary: One of the three large veins draining the liver into the inferior vena cava.

middle hepatic vein.summary: The hepatic vein running between the right and left halves of the liver.

splenic vein.summary: The vein from the spleen running behind the pancreas to join the superior mesenteric vein and form the portal vein.

superior mesenteric vein.summary: The vein draining the small intestine and right colon into the portal vein.

inferior mesenteric vein.summary: The vein draining the left colon and rectum, usually into the splenic vein.

renal vein.summary: The vein draining each kidney into the inferior vena cava; the left is longer and crosses in front of the aorta.

testicular vein.summary: The vein draining the testis; the right joins the vena cava, the left the renal vein.
testicular vein.clinical: Dilatation (varicocele) is commoner on the left.

common iliac vein.summary: The vein formed by the internal and external iliac veins; the two join to form the inferior vena cava.

external iliac vein.summary: The continuation of the femoral vein along the pelvic brim.

internal iliac vein.summary: The vein draining the pelvic organs and buttock.

femoral vein.summary: The main deep vein of the thigh, medial to the femoral artery.
femoral vein.clinical: The commonest site of deep vein thrombosis that leads to pulmonary embolism.

deep femoral vein.summary: The vein draining the thigh muscles into the femoral vein.

popliteal vein.summary: The deep vein behind the knee formed by the veins of the calf.

great saphenous vein.summary: The longest vein in the body, running up the inside of the leg and thigh from the foot to the groin.
great saphenous vein.clinical: Becomes varicose; often harvested for coronary bypass grafts.

small saphenous vein.summary: A superficial vein running up the back of the calf to the popliteal vein.

anterior tibial vein.summary: Deep veins accompanying the anterior tibial artery.

posterior tibial vein.summary: Deep veins accompanying the posterior tibial artery.
posterior tibial vein.clinical: A site of calf deep vein thrombosis.

fibular vein.summary: Deep veins accompanying the fibular artery.

superior pulmonary vein.summary: The upper of the two veins on each side carrying oxygenated blood from the lung to the left atrium.

inferior pulmonary vein.summary: The lower of the two pulmonary veins on each side, draining the lower lobe into the left atrium.

pulmonary artery.summary: The artery carrying deoxygenated blood from the pulmonary trunk to a lung.

intervertebral disk.summary: The fibrocartilage cushion between two vertebral bodies: a tough outer annulus fibrosus around a gel-like nucleus pulposus.
intervertebral disk.function: Absorbs shock and allows small movements between vertebrae.
intervertebral disk.clinical: Herniation can press on a nerve root, causing sciatica.

interosseous membrane of forearm.summary: The fibrous sheet joining the shafts of the radius and ulna.
interosseous membrane of forearm.function: Transfers load from the radius to the ulna and anchors the deep forearm muscles.

interosseous membrane of leg.summary: The fibrous sheet between the tibia and fibula.
interosseous membrane of leg.function: Binds the two bones and gives origin to leg muscles.

long plantar ligament.summary: The longest ligament of the sole, from the calcaneus to the bases of the metatarsals.
long plantar ligament.function: Supports the lateral arch of the foot.

stylohyoid ligament.summary: A fibrous cord from the styloid process to the lesser horn of the hyoid.
stylohyoid ligament.clinical: Calcification causes Eagle syndrome, a pain on swallowing.

lateral thyrohyoid ligament.summary: The thickened lateral edge of the thyrohyoid membrane.

median thyrohyoid ligament.summary: The thickened midline part of the thyrohyoid membrane.

sphenoid bone.summary: A butterfly-shaped bone in the centre of the skull base.
sphenoid bone.function: Its body holds the pituitary gland in the sella turcica and contains the sphenoidal sinus; its wings form parts of the orbit and skull.
sphenoid bone.clinical: Pituitary tumours are removed through the sphenoid (trans-sphenoidal surgery).

triquetral.summary: The three-cornered carpal bone on the little-finger side of the proximal row.
triquetral.function: Articulates with the pisiform and helps transmit force from the hand to the ulna side.

navicular bone of foot.summary: A boat-shaped tarsal bone on the inner side of the midfoot.
navicular bone of foot.function: Forms the highest point of the medial arch of the foot.
navicular bone of foot.clinical: Navicular stress fractures occur in athletes.

medial cuneiform bone.summary: The largest of the three wedge-shaped bones in front of the navicular.
medial cuneiform bone.function: Articulates with the first metatarsal and supports the medial arch.

intermediate cuneiform bone.summary: The smallest cuneiform, between the medial and lateral cuneiforms.

lateral cuneiform bone.summary: The outer of the three cuneiform bones.
lateral cuneiform bone.function: Supports the third metatarsal and contributes to the transverse arch.

brachiocephalic artery.summary: The first branch of the aortic arch, dividing into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

descending thoracic aorta.summary: The descending aorta as it runs down the chest beside the vertebral column.
descending thoracic aorta.function: Supplies the chest wall, oesophagus and bronchi through its branches.

descending aorta.summary: The aorta beyond the arch, descending through the chest and abdomen to its division at L4.
descending aorta.function: Supplies the chest wall, abdominal organs and lower limbs through its branches.
